spec_match.rationale: Shows the motivating bug — focus scrolling an unwanted axis — across three strip implementations including overflow: scroll clip.

interactive.rationale: Focus buttons drive real scroll-into-view; per-strip scroll offsets read back live.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The scroll-you-did-not-ask-for is demonstrated, not described.

edge_cases.rationale: Three authoring patterns compared, including the pre-feature workarounds.

conformance.rationale: The suite is correct, but on this 153 build the two core assertions fail: overflow: scroll clip is not yet honoured (clip computes away), so the feature branch of this demo runs the fallback — displayed honestly.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Focus-scroll measured live; the readouts matched the coerced (pre-feature) behaviour this build has; console clean.

accessibility.rationale: Buttons named, offsets textual, visible focus.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify once a build computes overflow: scroll clip per axis
openQuestions.detail: On Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 the pair computes to scroll/hidden (feature absent): conformance fails clip-survives-beside-a-scrollable-value and the-clipped-axis-stops-scrolling, and the demos show the coerced behaviour honestly. When a 153 stable (or later) build passes those two assertions, re-run the three concepts and refresh the critiques.

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 screenshots captured and inspected. Demo honest on a build that coerces scroll/clip to scroll/hidden; the suite correctly records the absence.
